(2.8 rpg) | stat3label = [[Assist (basketball)|Assists]] | stat3value = 1,105 (1.7 apg) | stats_league = NBA }} '''Avery Antonio Bradley Jr.''' (born November 26, 1990) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who is the vice president of player development for the [[Utah Jazz]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas Longhorns]] before being drafted 19th overall by the [[Boston Celtics]] in the [[2010 NBA draft]]. With the Celtics, Bradley was twice recognized as an [[NBA All-Defensive Team]] member. He also played for the [[Detroit Pistons]], [[Los Angeles Clippers]], [[Memphis Grizzlies]], [[Miami Heat]], [[Houston Rockets]] and [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. ==Early life== Bradley was born on November 26, 1990, in [[Tacoma, Washington]],{{Cite web |last=Quinn|first=Justin|title=On this day: Avery Bradley born; Delonte West debuts; Sherman Douglas traded to Bucks|url=https://celticswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/celtics/2024/11/26/celtics-history-bradley-born-west-debuts-douglas-traded-to-bucks/76465928007/|access-date=2025-06-03|website=Celtics Wire|language=en-US}}{{Cite web |title=Utah Jazz Hire Avery Bradley as Vice President of Player Development|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-hire-avery-bradley-as-vice-president-of-player-development|access-date=2025-06-03|website=NBA.com|language=en|date=2024-04-16}} to Avery Bradley Sr. and Alicia Jones-Bradley. He has two older brothers, and one older sister. Alicia worked in a welfare office, while Avery Sr. had a 22-year military career. After the two divorced in 2001, Bradley lived with his mother but maintained a strong relationship with his father, whose career took him all over the country.{{cite web |last1=Benbow |first1=Julian |title=Bradley already is well-connected |url=http://archive.boston.com/sports/basketball/celtics/articles/2010/07/04/new_celtic_bradley_already_is_well_connected/ |publisher=[[Boston.com]] |access-date=9 April 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151217165823/http://www.boston.com/sports/basketball/celtics/articles/2010/07/04/new_celtic_bradley_already_is_well_connected/ |archive-date=2015-12-17 |url-status=live}} Bradley became a [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas Longhorns]] fan when he lived in [[Arlington, Texas|Arlington]] from 2001 to 2004. Bradley and his family left Texas for Tacoma in the summer of 2004, before the start of his eighth grade year.{{cite web|title=Avery Bradley Stats, Video, Bio, Profile|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/avery_bradley/bio/|work=NBA.com|access-date=December 31, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151202025733/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/avery_bradley/bio/|archive-date=December 2, 2015|url-status=dead}} Bradley played on the same [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] team as future Celtics teammate [[Isaiah Thomas (basketball)|Isaiah Thomas]].[http://www.celticslife.com/2015/02/avery-bradley-and-isaiah-thomas-share.html/ Avery Bradley and Isaiah Thomas share a childhood connection] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150709054256/http://www.celticslife.com/2015/02/avery-bradley-and-isaiah-thomas-share.html/|date=July 9, 2015}} ==High school career== Bradley was ranked among the top high school basketball players in the class of 2009. [[ESPNU]] 100 rated him No. 1 nationally,{{Cite web |title=Avery Bradley ESPN Recruiting Profile - Class of 2009 |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/52214 |access-date=2026-07-03 |website=ESPN.com}} and he was rated No. 4 by [[Rivals.com]][https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Avery-Bradley-60888 AVERY BRADLEY – Yahoo] and No. 5 by [[Scout.com]].[http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=8&c=1&nid=3126715 Avery Bradley Player Profile News] Bradley propelled [[The Henderson International School|Findlay College Prep]] to the National High School Basketball championship game against [[Oak Hill Academy (Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]], winning the contest 56–53. After leading Findlay to the title, Bradley was named National High School Basketball Player of the Year by [[Parade (magazine)|Parade Magazine]]. He played against the nation's best high school players at the 2009 [[McDonald's All-American Game]] and won the McDonald's All-American Dunk Contest. Before transferring to Findlay Prep for his senior campaign, Bradley was a three-year starter at [[Bellarmine Preparatory School]] in Tacoma, Washington. Bradley and [[University of Washington]] recruit [[Abdul Gaddy]] led Bellarmine Prep to the Class 4A State Semifinals with a 25–4 mark as a junior.[http://www.texassports.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=210 AVERY BRADLEY - 2009-10 MEN'S BASKETBALL] ==College career== Bradley attended the [[University of Texas at Austin]]. He found the [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas Longhorns basketball]] program appealing in part because he had spent parts of his childhood in [[Arlington, Texas|Arlington]], where Bradley became a fan of [[T. J. Ford]].{{cite web |url=http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/tex/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/121809_dmn.pdf|title=Freshman Avery Bradley is fulfilling a childhood dream with spot on Texas Longhorns, big game in Arlington|date=December 18, 2009|publisher=Dallas Morning News|first=Kate|last=Hairopoulos|access-date=December 9, 2014|archive-date=December 16, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141216024208/http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/tex/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/121809_dmn.pdf|url-status=dead}} As a freshman in 2009–10, Bradley averaged 11.6 points for the Longhorns and established himself as one of the top defensive guards in the country.{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20141209124911/http://www.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/texas-freshman-avery-bradley-to-test-draft-waters-040610|title=Texas freshman to test NBA waters}} He subsequently earned Big 12 All-Rookie Team and All-Big 12 Honorable Mention honors. In April 2010, Bradley declared for the [[NBA draft]], forgoing his final three years of college eligibility.[https://www.sbnation.com/2010/4/6/2314700/texas-avery-bradley-declares-for-nba-draft-wont-sign-with-agent Texas' Avery Bradley Declares For NBA Draft, Won't Sign With Agent] ==Professional career== ===Boston Celtics (2010–2011)=== [[File:Avery_Bradley_and_Jordan_Crawford.jpg|left|thumb|Bradley defending [[Jordan Crawford]] in 2011]] Bradley was selected with the 19th overall pick in the [[2010 NBA draft]] by the [[Boston Celtics]]. On July 2, 2010, he signed his rookie-scale contract with the Celtics.{{Cite web |last=Forsberg |first=Chris |date=2010-07-02 |title=C's sign Avery Bradley |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/boston/celtics/post/_/id/4675595 |access-date=2026-07-03 |website=ESPN.com}} The same day, Bradley underwent successful ankle surgery and subsequently missed the 2010 NBA Summer League.[https://web.archive.org/web/20100706175229/http://www.boston.com/sports/basketball/celtics/extras/celtics_blog/2010/07/bradley_signs_h.html Bradley signs, has surgery] Still just 19 years old, Bradley joined a Celtics team that was one of the best in the [[Eastern Conference (NBA)|Eastern Conference]]. He did not see his first regular-season action until the fourteenth game of the season, a 23-point victory over the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in which Bradley scored two points and committed two turnovers.[https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4240/year/2011 Avery Bradley Game-by-Game Stats (2010-11)] On January 14, 2011, Bradley was assigned to the [[Maine Red Claws]] of the [[NBA Development League]] and on the same day made his debut game for the team, playing 21 minutes and scoring 11 points.{{Cite web |last=Forsberg |first=Chris |date=2011-01-14 |title=Bradley assigned to D-League |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/boston/celtics/post/_/id/4679627 |access-date=2026-07-03 |website=ESPN.com}} Following a [[spinal cord]] injury to [[Marquis Daniels]] during a game against the [[Orlando Magic]] on February 6, Bradley was recalled by the Celtics the next day and joined the team for the game against the [[Charlotte Bobcats]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.celticstown.com/2011/02/07/avery-bradley-recalled-from-d-league/|title=Avery Bradley recalled from D-League|access-date=December 9, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141214201208/http://www.celticstown.com/2011/02/07/avery-bradley-recalled-from-d-league/|archive-date=December 14, 2014|url-status=usurped}} In the one Celtics game of Bradley's rookie season in which he played more than 15 minutes, Bradley scored 20 points to go with three rebounds, two assists and two steals. However, he played 10 or more minutes in just two other NBA games and did not appear in any of the Celtics' postseason contests. On June 30, 2011, the Celtics exercised their third-year team option on Bradley's rookie-scale contract, extending the contract through the 2012–13 season.[http://nesn.com/2011/06/celtics-exercise-contract-option-on-avery-bradley-for-2012-13-season/ Celtics Exercise Contract Option on Avery Bradley for 2012-13 Season] ===Hapoel Jerusalem (2011)=== In October 2011, Bradley signed with [[Hapoel Jerusalem B.C.|Hapoel Jerusalem]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]] for the duration of the [[2011 NBA lockout|NBA lockout]].{{Cite web |last=Forsberg |first=Chris |date=2011-10-06 |title=Bradley signs to play in Israel |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/boston/celtics/post/_/id/4686434 |access-date=2026-07-03 |website=ESPN.com}} He played three games with the team, averaging 13.7 points per game. === Return to Boston (2011–2017) === ==== 2011–12 season ==== [[File:Avery_Bradley_layup.jpg|thumb|Bradley going up for a layup in 2012]] During the [[2011–12 NBA season]], Bradley enjoyed much more playing time and was promoted to a starting role following an injury to [[Ray Allen]]. Bradley's scoring output increased significantly during the season, and he managed a career-high 28 points against the [[Atlanta Hawks]] on April 20, 2012. He also received praise for his tremendous hustle and defense, including memorable blocks on [[Dwyane Wade]] and [[Russell Westbrook]], among others. However, Bradley suffered a [[dislocated shoulder]] during the [[2012 NBA playoffs]]. This injury, which led to season-ending surgery, was a significant setback to the Celtics, who lost in seven games to the [[Miami Heat]] in the Conference Finals. ====2012–13 season==== On October 30, 2012, the Celtics exercised their fourth-year team option on Bradley's rookie-scale contract, extending the contract through the 2013–14 season.[http://nesn.com/2012/10/celtics-exercise-fourth-year-option-on-guard-avery-bradley/ Celtics Exercise Fourth-Year Option on Guard Avery Bradley] With Bradley still sidelined for the beginning of the [[2012–13 NBA season]], the aging Celtics struggled with the duo of [[Courtney Lee]] and [[Jason Terry]] receiving the majority of minutes at [[shooting guard]]. On January 2, 2013, Bradley returned to action against the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], regaining his spot as the starting [[shooting guard]] and providing a significant boost to the team, evident by their winning six out of Bradley's first seven games back. However, the season was ultimately a disappointment for both Bradley and the Celtics. Although he led the league in fewest points per play allowed on defense, at 0.697,{{Cite web |last=Forsberg |first=Chris |date=2013-05-05 |title=Avery Bradley's sudden redemption |url=https://www.espn.com/boston/nba/story/_/id/9244474 |access-date=2026-07-03 |website=ESPN.com}} Bradley struggled offensively, shooting just 40.2 percent from the field and managing 15 or more points just five times in 50 regular-season games. The Celtics lost any realistic chance of contention after point guard [[Rajon Rondo]] went down with a [[torn ACL]] on January 27,{{Cite web |last=Forsberg |first=Chris |date=2013-01-27 |others=Contributed by Jackie MacMullan and The Associated Press |title=Celtics' Rajon Rondo has torn ACL |url=https://www.espn.com/boston/nba/story/_/id/8887106 |access-date=2026-07-03 |website=ESPN.com}} leaving them without their most dynamic player. After falling behind three games to none against the [[New York Knicks]] in the first round of the playoffs, Boston mounted a furious comeback, winning two games and narrowly losing Game 6. Bradley, whose play in the series had mirrored the ineffectiveness of the team, provided a gutsy effort at the end of the game, making all four of his shots and stealing the ball three times in the last ten minutes. The Celtics entered the offseason with an eye toward the future and Bradley a vital part of their plans to rebuild a contender. ====2013–14 season==== The Celtics ended an era on the day of the [[2013 NBA draft]], trading aging stars [[Kevin Garnett]] and [[Paul Pierce]], as well as [[Jason Terry]] and [[D. J. White]], to the [[Brooklyn Nets]]. The Celtics also declined to sign Bradley to a contract extension before the October 31, 2013, deadline, allowing him to become a restricted free agent in 2014.{{cite web|url=http://www.celticslife.com/2013/11/avery-bradley-celtics-fail-to-work-out.html|title=Avery Bradley, Celtics fail to work out extension – Bradley will become restricted free agent next summer|work=CelticsLife.com|date=November 1, 2013|access-date=December 9, 2014}} However, new Celtics coach [[Brad Stevens]] professed his trust in Bradley, who, in the absence of the injured Rondo, began the [[2013–14 NBA season]] as the team's starting point guard. Bradley's time at point guard lasted just four disappointing games; he had more turnovers than assists, and the Celtics lost all four times.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/bradlav01/gamelog/2014/|title=Avery Bradley 2013-14 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=December 9, 2014}} In an effort to turn the team around, Stevens named [[Jordan Crawford]] the new point guard, allowing Bradley to move to his natural shooting guard. The move worked brilliantly, as the Celtics immediately went on a four-game winning streak and the more comfortable Bradley settled nicely into his role on the team.{{cite web|last=Robb|first=Brian|url=http://boston.cbslocal.com/2013/12/31/robb-avery-bradley-progressing-into-one-of-nbas-most-well-rounded-guards/|title=Robb: Avery Bradley Progressing Into One Of NBA's Most Well-Rounded Guards|work=cbslocal.com|date=December 31, 2013|access-date=December 9, 2014}} Although the Celtics' lack of talent and experience began to show itself as the season went along, particularly with Rondo still out, Bradley was a rare bright spot, increasing his scoring average every month through January. Bradley was especially effective in December, shooting a fantastic 50 percent on three-pointers and making 48.7 percent of his shots overall. Unfortunately, on January 21, in just the third game all season that Rondo was active, Bradley sprained his ankle{{cite web|last=Holmes|first=Baxter|url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/sports/2014/01/22/avery-bradley-out-early-with-injured-ankle/7eU1TDBolnO3uv8juwM3gL/story.html|title=Avery Bradley out early with injured ankle|work=BostonGlobe.com|date=January 22, 2014|access-date=December 9, 2014}} and ended up missing five games. Shortly after returning, on February 5, Bradley re-sprained the same ankle. Determined to be cautious, Stevens still had not set a return date for Bradley as the Celtics headed into the All-Star break more than a week later.{{cite web|last=Washburn|first=Gary|url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/sports/2014/02/12/celtics-avery-bradley-out-indefinitely-with-ankle-injury/vsSegJw07ZgV9hpaYVC6qO/story.html|title=Celtics' Avery Bradley out indefinitely with ankle injury|work=BostonGlobe.com|date=February 13, 2014|access-date=December 9, 2014}} Bradley ultimately returned to action on March 14. In his fourth game back, a victory over the Miami Heat, Bradley connected on a career-high six three-pointers as part of a 23-point effort,[http://www.nba.com/games/20140319/MIABOS/gameinfo.html Notebook: Celtics 101, Heat 96] then followed it up with 28 points, matching his career high, the next game.[http://bostonherald.com/sports/celtics_nba/celtics_insider/2014/03/bradleys_career_high_cant_keep_celtics_from_road_loss_to Bradley's career high can't keep Celtics from road loss to Nets] When healthy, Bradley played significant minutes and played effectively in the final stretch of the season, scoring at least 18 points in the team's last five games. He shouldered a higher percentage of the offensive workload for Celtics in 2013–14, and Bradley responded by greatly improving his shooting from the previous season. In a rebuilding year for the team, one that saw them win only 25 games, Bradley stood out as one of their few consistent performers. ====2014–15 season==== With Bradley set to become a restricted free agent in July 2014, the Celtics needed to extend a qualifying offer of $3.6 million in order to be able to match any contract offered by another team, which they did on June 30.[http://nesn.com/2014/06/celtics-extend-qualifying-offer-to-restricted-free-agent-avery-bradley/ Celtics Extend Qualifying Offer To Restricted Free Agent Avery Bradley] On July 15, Bradley re-signed with the Celtics{{Cite web |last=D'Amico |first=Marc |date=2014-07-15 |title=Celtics Re-Sign Avery Bradley |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-re-sign-avery-bradley |access-date=2026-07-03 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} to a four-year, $32 million contract.{{Cite web |last=Forsberg |first=Chris |date=2015-07-02 |title=Avery Bradley to stay with Celtics |url=https://www.espn.com/boston/nba/story/_/id/11167031 |access-date=2026-07-03 |website=ESPN.com}}{{Cite web |last=Bulpett |first=Steve |date=2014-07-02 |title=Celtics Agree To Four-Year, $32M Deal With Avery Bradley |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/234082/Celtics-Agree-To-Four-Year-$32M-Deal-With-Avery-Bradley |access-date=2026-07-03 |publisher=Boston Herald |language=en |via=basketball.realgm.com}} Although the Celtics had high hopes for their backcourt pairing of Bradley and Rajon Rondo, both now healthy, they were soon dealt a setback when Rondo broke his hand a month before the 2014–15 season.{{Cite news |last=Holmes |first=Baxter |date=2014-09-30 |title=Rajon Rondo describes breaking hand |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/sports/2014/09/29/rajon-rondo-broke-his-hand-falling-shower/J90WkqDnMd9MsTxvKbISUJ/story.html |access-date=2026-07-03 |work=The Boston Globe |language=en-US |issn=0743-1791}} Although the team planned to be cautious with Rondo's injury, Brad Stevens made the decision to keep Bradley at shooting guard even with Rondo out, with a mix of rookie [[Marcus Smart]], second-year guard [[Phil Pressey]] and new acquisition [[Evan Turner]] playing point guard.{{Cite news |last=Washburn |first=Gary |date=2014-10-01 |title=In pointed decision, Avery Bradley now a shooting guard |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/sports/2014/09/30/pointed-decision-avery-bradley-now-shooting-guard/9jcNRt8gz8owF3ebLfzchN/story.html |access-date=2026-07-03 |work=The Boston Globe |language=en-US |issn=0743-1791}} Despite the concerns, Rondo ultimately surprised many by being ready for opening night. Bradley continued to play harassing defense and scored in double digits in 13 of the team's first 15 games,{{Cite web |title=Avery Bradley 2014-15 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/bradlav01/gamelog/2015/ |access-date=2026-07-03 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}} including a career-high 32 points in a loss to the [[Dallas Mavericks]].[http://www.nba.com/games/20141103/BOSDAL/gameinfo.html Parsons, Mavs hold on to beat Celtics 118-113] However, the Celtics struggled to a 4–11 start. Meanwhile, Bradley's offense cooled off in December, as he shot just 39 percent from the field for that month and made just 1-of-21 three-point attempts over a six-game stretch. Faced with a 9–14 record on December 18, Celtics president of basketball operations [[Danny Ainge]] made the difficult decision to part with Rondo, trading him and rookie [[Dwight Powell]] to the Dallas Mavericks for [[Brandan Wright]], [[Jae Crowder]], [[Jameer Nelson]] and two draft picks.{{Cite web |url=http://www.mavs.com/mavs-acquire-rajon-rondo-dwight-powell-from-celtics/|title=Mavs acquire four-time All-Star Rajon Rondo|access-date=November 5, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141219043216/http://www.mavs.com/mavs-acquire-rajon-rondo-dwight-powell-from-celtics/|archive-date=December 19, 2014|url-status=dead|website=mavs.com|date=2014-12-18}} Pundits such as [[Bill Simmons]] and [[Jalen Rose]] portrayed the trade as a surrender to a mediocrity, with the hopes of getting a high draft pick at season's end,[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fydMDILqnx4/ Bill and Jalen React To The Rondo Trade] and the Celtics continued to struggle after Rondo's exit. However, under the tutelage of Brad Stevens, and with the help of trade acquisition [[Isaiah Thomas (basketball)|Isaiah Thomas]],{{Cite web |date=2015-02-19 |title=Celtics Acquire Thomas From Phoenix |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-acquire-thomas-phoenix |access-date=2026-07-03 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} the young Celtics gradually improved. After failing to post winning records in November, December or January, they did so in February, March and April, and won eight of the season's last nine games.{{Cite web |title=2014-15 Boston Celtics Team Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/BOS/2015/gamelog/ |access-date=2026-07-03 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}} Bradley's offensive output was especially effective in February, as he managed over 18 points per game in the month while shooting 47 percent from the field and over 40 percent from three-point range.{{Cite web |title=Avery Bradley 2014-15 Game Log |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4240/year/2015 |access-date=2026-07-03 |website=ESPN.com}} Although a shoulder injury sidelined him for three games between March 6 and 9, he returned to score 17 points against the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] on March 11. For the regular season, Bradley led the Celtics in minutes played and points,[https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/BOS/2015.html/ 2014-15 Boston Celtics Roster and Stats] although his points per game and shooting percentages declined slightly from 2013 to 2014.[https://www.espn.com/nba/player/stats/_/id/4240 Avery Bradley Stats] A 40–42 record saw the Celtics earn the #7 seed in the Eastern Conference. Their playoff series was brief, as the eventual Eastern Conference champion [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] swept the Celtics in four games. Bradley played 40 out of the 48 minutes in the last game of the series, but his 16 points was not enough to overcome [[LeBron James]] and the Cavaliers. Nevertheless, the 2014–15 season was a surprise success for the Celtics and another solid year, and a relatively healthy year, for Bradley. ====2015–16 season==== Fresh off of their first playoff appearance in the [[Brad Stevens]] era, the Celtics entered 2015–16 campaign eager to prove that it had not been a fluke. Acquiring veteran forwards [[David Lee (basketball)|David Lee]] and [[Amir Johnson]] to fortify their frontcourt, the team also hoped to see the continued improvement of their promising young players, including [[Marcus Smart]] and [[Jared Sullinger]]. They started the year off slow, winning just one of their first four. Bradley provided a rare highlight, however, throwing down a tremendous dunk on reigning [[NBA Defensive Player of the Year|Defensive Player of the Year]] [[Kawhi Leonard]].[http://nba.nbcsports.com/2015/11/02/avery-bradley-drives-past-kawhi-leonard-throws-down-huge-dunk-video/ Avery Bradley drives past Kawhi Leonard, throws down huge dunk] After missing two games with a calf injury, Bradley returned to action as a [[sixth man]] after starting 224 of 226 Celtics games in which he was healthy. Bradley excelled in his new role, improving his scoring, efficiency and defensive rating.{{Cite web |last=Forsberg |first=Chris |date=2015-11-21 |title=Something in reserve: Avery Bradley thrives off bench, but for how long? |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/boston/celtics/post/_/id/4721055 |access-date=2026-07-03 |website=ESPN.com}} He soon returned to the starting lineup on November 22 and proved himself highly capable in either role, immediately managing two games in a row with at least 25 points and 13 in a row with at least 10 points. Bradley missed three games in early January with a hip injury,[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/bradlav01/gamelog/2016/ Avery Bradley 2015-16 Game Log] and upon his return, the Celtics emerged as one of the top teams in the Eastern Conference. Bradley contributed a number of memorable performances. On January 27, he scored 21 of his season-high-tying 27 points in the first half of a 111–103 victory over the Denver Nuggets.[http://www.nba.com/games/20160127/DENBOS/gameinfo.html Bradley matches season-high 27, Celtics down Nuggets 111-103] Eight days later, Bradley connected on a game-winning three-pointer to give Boston a narrow 104–103 victory over the Eastern Conference-leading Cleveland Cavaliers.[http://www.nba.com/games/20160205/BOSCLE/gameinfo.html Bradley's 3-pointer at horn gives Celtics 104-103 win][https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=__ljBiuA8RU Avery Bradley Hits the Game Winner in Cleveland!] On February 29, he blocked a shot from [[Utah Jazz]] forward [[Gordon Hayward]] with 23 seconds left in the game to give the Celtics a victory.{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20160928015743/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=400828773/|title=Celtics' home streak reaches 11 with 100-95 win over Jazz}} For the season, Bradley was his team's second leading scorer, behind only All-Star [[Isaiah Thomas (basketball)|Isaiah Thomas]]. With a 48–34 record, the Celtics finished the regular season in a four-way tie for the third seed in Eastern Conference and were assigned the fifth seed based on tiebreaker rules. Drawing the Atlanta Hawks in the first round of the playoffs, the Celtics narrowly lost in Game 1, as Bradley scored 18 points but went down in the fourth quarter with an apparent right hamstring injury.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160416/BOSATL/gameinfo.html|title=Hawks hold off another Celtics rally, take Game 1 102-101|work=NBA.com|date=April 16, 2016|access-date=April 26, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160426210424/http://www.nba.com/games/20160416/BOSATL/gameinfo.html|archive-date=April 26, 2016|url-status=dead}} The injury turned out to be serious enough to sideline Bradley for the rest of the series,{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160426/BOSATL/gameinfo.html|title=With big turnaround, Hawks beat Celtics 110-83 for 3-2 lead|work=NBA.com|date=April 26, 2016|access-date=April 26, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160428005426/http://www.nba.com/games/20160426/BOSATL/gameinfo.html|archive-date=April 28, 2016|url-status=dead}} which turned out to be a crippling blow for the Celtics. They were considerably outplayed by the Hawks in his absence, particularly on offense, and lost the series in six games. However, Bradley's sixth NBA season was both an individual and team success, capped off when he was included in the [[NBA All-Defensive First Team]].[http://www.nba.com/2016/news/05/25/san-antonio-spurs-kawhi-leonard-unanimous-selection-for-all-defensive-first-team/ Leonard, Green headline All-Defensive First Team] ====2016–17 season==== Bradley and the Celtics both continued to improve in 2016–17. Beginning with an opening night 17-point performance that included 3-of-4 three-point shooting, Bradley enjoyed his most effective offensive season, although injuries limited him to just 55 games. Starting every game he played, Bradley was remarkably consistent, with double-digit scoring in 50 of his 55 regular-season contests.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4240/year/2017 |title=Avery Bradley Game-by-Game Stats 2016-17 |work=ESPN.com|access-date=July 11, 2017}} At his best, Bradley was an outstanding weapon from three-point range. In the Celtics' third game of the season, for instance, he scored 31 points on a career-high eight three-pointers, also managing 11 rebounds, as the Celtics defeated the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899477|title=Bradley hits 8 3s, Celtics beat Hornets 104-98|work=ESPN.com|date=October 29, 2016|access-date=October 30, 2016}} Bradley's season scoring average of 16.3 points per game was a career high, while his 39.0 three-point percentage was his best since 2013–14. Bradley's rebounding totals, meanwhile, saw a dramatic leap, as he averaged 6.1 for the season, nearly double what he ever had before. Bradley managed double-digit rebounds on 10 occasions, including November 16, when he recorded a career-high 13, to go along with 18 points, in a victory over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/celtics-avery-bradley-grabs-career-high-13-rebounds-in-wednesdays-win/|title=Celtics' Avery Bradley: Grabs career-high 13 rebounds in Wednesday's win|work=CBSSports.com|date=November 17, 2016|access-date=December 8, 2016}} Unfortunately, Bradley struggled through several injuries, most notably a right Achilles injury that cost him 22 out of 23 games during a stretch in January and February.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900291|title=Hawks prevail 114-98 in scrappy showdown with Celtics|work=ESPN.com|date=February 27, 2017|access-date=February 27, 2017}} The season was a success for the Celtics, as a 53–29 record earned them the No. 1 seed in the Eastern Conference playoffs.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/19146112|title=Celtics to face Bulls in opening round; Cavaliers get Pacers|work=ESPN.com|date=April 13, 2017|access-date=July 13, 2017}} However, in the first round of the postseason, the Celtics initially struggled and fell behind the eighth-seeded [[Chicago Bulls]] 2–0. When they managed to win the series in six games, it marked Bradley and the team's first postseason series win since 2012.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400950389|title=Bradley scores 23, Celtics eliminate Bulls 105-83|work=ESPN.com|date=April 28, 2017|access-date=April 29, 2017}} Bradley scored 24 and 23 points in Games 5 and 6, with the 24 points a playoff career high.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400950387|title=Celtics beat Bulls 108-97, take 3-2 lead in series|work=ESPN.com|date=April 26, 2017|access-date=April 27, 2017}} He topped that in the next round, with 29 points against the [[Washington Wizards]] in Game 5 to help the Celtics take a 3–2 lead in the series, which they ultimately won in seven games.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400952530|title=Bradley scores 29, Celtics power past Wizards, 123-101|work=ESPN.com|date=May 10, 2017|access-date=May 10, 2017}} The Celtics' Eastern Conference Finals opponent, the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], ultimately proved to be too much. In an otherwise one-sided series, the high point for the Celtics came courtesy of Bradley. Playing Game 3 down two games to none and without the injured [[Isaiah Thomas (basketball)|Isaiah Thomas]], Boston stayed unexpectedly close to the Cavaliers throughout the game, then won when Bradley's 3-pointer bounced around the rim and fell with less than a second left. Bradley finished the game with 20 points.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400953696|title=Bradley hits last-second shot, Celtics stun Cavs 111-108|work=ESPN.com|date=May 21, 2017|access-date=May 21, 2017}} The Celtics lost both the fourth and fifth games, bowing out of the playoffs. ===Detroit Pistons (2017–2018)=== On July 7, 2017, in a bid to clear enough cap space to (including 45 starts) for Los Angeles, recording averages of 6.4 points, 2.2 rebounds, and 0.8 assists. ==Player profile== Although he had a build more typical of a [[point guard]], Bradley played the [[shooting guard]] position. Making up for his lack of size at the position with quickness, strength and tenacity, Bradley excelled at defense. Opponents [[Damian Lillard]] and [[CJ McCollum]] called him the best perimeter defender in the NBA.[http://www.masslive.com/celtics/index.ssf/2016/04/damian_lillard_boston_celtics.html/ Damian Lillard told Boston Celtics guard Avery Bradley he's the NBA's best perimeter defender][https://twitter.com/CJMcCollum/status/716107313891778560 Avery Bradley the best perimeter defender in the...] Bradley had outstanding athleticism and explosiveness, having won the Slam Dunk Contest at the 2009 [[McDonald's All-American Game]]. However, he rarely displayed his elite leaping ability in games, occasionally blocking players at the rim or throwing down dunks but more often simply harassing his man on the perimeter and settling for layups. Bradley's intense and frenetic defensive style of play, probably his most valuable asset, may also be partly to blame for the series of injuries he has suffered in his career. However, Bradley's most serious injuries, which required three surgeries by the time he was 23,[http://www.foxsports.com/nba/story/boston-celtics-avery-bradley-contract-unhappy-fire-agent-012616/ Celtics' Bradley fires agent, is reportedly unhappy with contract] happened early in his career. Due to his defense and his offensive improvement, Bradley became an increasingly important member of the Celtics during his tenure there, and his minutes played per game steadily increased over his
